summary: The CSS half and the CSS-to-JS gap are fixed, and the font preload is in place for standard (node-served) builds. Feature stylesheets now load with their lazy chunks: main CSS went from about 601 KB to 515,012 B raw, and from 79 KiB to 66.8 KB gzip. I found no keyframe or selector collisions and no unstyled callers outside the owning chunks. The font preload is deliberately left out of hosted-hub builds (app.ryco.space), and a test pins that. The stated reason is that the Hub surface has its own typography, which is wrong: the hosted document and every Hub component paint in DM Sans, and the hosted build's own service-worker code precaches DM Sans as the font the boot document paints with. So a cold hosted load still requests DM Sans only when the shell commits text, and the post-paint swap remains there. Warm hosted loads are mostly covered by the service-worker precache.

evidence.note: The projects, pullRequests, automations and overview @imports are gone. Only pullRequests/styles/rail.css stays global, for the sidebar workspace PR popover (12 .pr-swap rules are still in main CSS).

Imports ./projects.css. PullRequestsPage.tsx:2, workspace/WorkspacePullRequestPanel.tsx:2, automations/dialog/AutomationsDialog.tsx:2 and overview/crown/CrownOverview.tsx:2 import their sheets the same way.
A test pins the feature-stylesheet owners, keeps index.css free of the four sheets, and keeps rail.css global.
Dynamic imports keep their full dependency list, including CSS, so __vitePreload waits for the per-chunk CSS before the lazy component resolves. No unstyled flash and no missing CSS.

Build from Oct 14, after HEAD's commit time. 515,012 B raw and 66,777 B gzip, versus 587 KiB / 79 KiB in the report. No .crown-, .ad-dialog, .pk-, .projects-, .map-card, .pr-list or .notes-pane selectors. Per-chunk CSS: AutomationsDialog 33.7 KB, ChatOverviewPanel 21.2 KB, ProjectsRouteView 12.9 KB, usePullRequestsModel 11.8 KB (shared by the PR page and the workspace PR panel).

Every class defined in the moved sheets is used only inside its feature directory. RollingText's base rules stay in index.css:3017+, and only the crown overrides moved. No @keyframes name or selector duplicates index.css, and the moved files have no @apply, @layer or @reference, so changing cascade order and processing them separately is safe.

Modulepreload hints for boot, rolldown-runtime, boot-vendor and main JS, a style preload for main CSS, and a font preload for dm-sans-latin-wght-normal-Xz1IZZA0.woff2 with crossorigin. The woff2 matches the URL in main CSS. Main JS no longer waits for the CSS download.
createBootFontPreloadPlugin injects the hashed font preload through transformIndexHtml post.
The font preload is registered only when resolvedClientMode === 'standard'. The comment justifies this with 'the Hub surface has its own typography'.
The test pins that hosted-hub builds do NOT get ryco-boot-font-preload.

--font-family-sans defaults to "DM Sans", and body uses it at index.css:722-723. No :root[data-surface="hub"] rule overrides the font. Hub components (components/hostedHub/**) set no custom font family.
The boot <style> in the shared index.html sets body font-family to "DM Sans" in hosted builds too.

The hosted PWA plugin precaches findBootFontAsset() as a bootDocumentAssets entry (line 395-400), described as the font the boot document paints with (the default UI face). This contradicts the vite.config rationale.
On origin/main, the Hub builds vendor/ryco apps/web with VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE=hosted-hub and serves that dist itself. The hosted SPA is the same DM Sans app.

remaining: Hosted-hub builds have no DM Sans preload: vite.config.ts:132-134 registers createBootFontPreloadPlugin only for standard builds, and viteConfig.test.ts:133 pins that. The hosted index.html (app.ryco.space) therefore finds DM Sans only when the shell commits text, and cold loads such as a first visit or a new browser get the post-paint font swap the finding describes. Warm hosted loads are largely covered by the service-worker precache of the font (buildArtifacts.ts:395-400), which serves it from Cache Storage within milliseconds. Also minor: in all builds the preload is unconditional, so users who picked another sans face (Geist, Inter and so on) download 36 KiB of DM Sans for nothing.
fixDefects: The CSS move and the CSS/JS waterfall have no functional defects. The defect is in the font preload: the comment at vite.config.ts:129-131 says the Hub surface has its own typography, but the hosted surface renders in DM Sans (index.css:506, index.html:34-43, buildArtifacts.ts:144), so the hosted build was wrongly excluded and a test (viteConfig.test.ts:133) locks the exclusion in.
implementationSketch: 1) apps/web/vite.config.ts:127-134: register createBootFontPreloadPlugin() for both client modes and keep only createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin() behind resolvedClientMode === 'standard'. Rewrite the comment (CDN compression is still a valid reason for the precompressed plugin, but not for the font). 2) apps/web/src/viteConfig.test.ts:126-134: expect ryco-boot-font-preload in pluginNames('hosted-hub') too. 3) Check that the hosted index.html transform in pwa/buildArtifacts.ts (inline-script hashing, boot document, offline.html) accepts an extra <link> tag; 3ce80cee6 already adds modulepreload and style-preload links to hosted builds. Check that the preload href (config.base + fileName) equals the precached bootDocumentAssets URL (pathAtBase(publicBase, fileName)), so the service worker serves both from one cache entry. Optionally add the same preload to renderHostedPwaOfflineDocument. 4) Validate: build hosted mode into a scratch worktree (VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE=hosted-hub bun run --cwd apps/web build) and assert dist/index.html carries <link rel=preload as=font type=font/woff2 crossorigin href=/assets/dm-sans-latin-wght-normal-*.woff2>. Re-run the 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps and 10 Mbps hosted sign-in profile from 3ce80cee6 (4.81 s / 1.33 s baselines) and confirm the DM Sans request now starts at document start, the sign-in text paints without a swap, and sign-in time does not regress from 36 KiB of high-priority bandwidth contention. 5) To reach users, a Hub vendor-pin bump and deploy. 6) Optional: emit the preload from the inline head script only when the persisted appearance preference is the default sans face, so non-default users don't pay 36 KiB.
decisionReason: Including the hosted build reverses a deliberate, test-pinned exclusion. It changes the hosted index.html that app.ryco.space serves, so it only reaches users through a Hub vendor-pin bump and deploy. It also trades about 36 KiB of early high-priority bandwidth against the boot chain on slow links, where the hosted team has measured sign-in carefully. That trade-off should be confirmed with the slow-link profile before shipping.
